summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (113/47)

data.turoyo: Komər hano stene fayəš bi mamlakayḏe, d mamlaxle, fayəš məqdar, məlle: "Bawo, i ḥurmayḏe l ḥal ḥreno wa."
data.translation: Er blieb eine Zeitlang in seinem Lande, da, wo er König geworden war, da dachte er: Meine Frau war doch in anderen Umständen.

rationale: First III Preterit box example; retains existing ruling sense and contextual accession interpretation.

data.turoyo: Əno malko w məlaxno ʕal i walaye kula, aydarbo kəmmatli "əno nafəl lebi bi barṯo du baqorano"?
data.translation: ich bin der König über diese ganze Stadt, wie kannst du mir sagen 'mein Herz ist in die Tochter dieses Kuhhirten gefallen'
data.ref: Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/6

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell; first-person form and explicit territory despite the edition's condensed rendering.

data.turoyo: Maḥətla u toġo dam malke b qarʕa du gawro, lə mawḏaʕla li walaye, u gawro mvayəʕ, w hiye kməlxo w hiye kḥəkmo.
data.translation: (In der zwischen Zeit) setzt (die Frau) die Krone der Könige, ihres Mannes, auf ihren Haupt, sie ließ niemanden wissen, daß ihr Mann verschwand und sie regierte.
data.ref: Bilgic Lieber einen Gesellen als einen Prinzen/34

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell; female ruler, coordinated with kḥəkmo.

data.turoyo: More du ṣabr u malko d Məṣər, kmoləx ʕal i arʕo kula.
data.translation: Der Geduldige und der König von Aegypten sind Herren über die ganze Erde;

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell; different attested context for a reference already listed, with overt whole-earth domain.

data.turoyo: Ayna d kətwa Hetim, bu waxt diḏe, u rabo daṭ Ṭaye we w mamlaxwa ʕal aṭ Ṭaya, saymiwa ḥas mene.
data.translation: Hatim war zu seiner Zeit der Herr der Taiyiten. Er herrschte über sie und war bei ihnen sehr beliebt.

rationale: Thin III Infectum-wa cell; complete short context and ʕal-governed people.

summary: I marks governed people or territory with ʕal. III also has ʕal at 111/3 and a direct suffixed kingdom theme at inherited 112/2; it is not uniformly causative in these attestations.

New III Preterit mamlaxle at 113/47 has contextual accession/anterior force in a relative clause. Existing herrschen covers the use; German König geworden does not alone establish a new inchoative sense.
The Bilgic feminine kməlxo and first-person məlaxno broaden form coverage without changing meaning. III Infectum-wa gives continuing rule in 111/3.
Read-only lookup of mlk confirms its parallel rule/accession senses and first-person example. Retain mlx as assigned; consonant spelling and existing paradigms should be coordinated editorially.

PrS 58/89 is the inherited throne example; 112/2 is the inherited III example. PrS 86/52 has a different maxim already included among the inherited references, so print only its newly supplied context without treating the reference as new.
Interpret More du ṣabr u malko d Məṣər before singular kmoləx at PrS 86/52; do not infer a new subject-agreement paradigm from the edition’s plural translation.
Should mlk and mlx be cross-referenced or combined as variants? The supplied evidence does not authorise merging their entries.
Is the fragmented dmamlaxwa clause at MAC Ishaq Material culture/35 accurately transcribed? Rule is clear, but it is a poorer example than 111/3 and is withheld.
Restore the missing e in German 'liebreich'
rationale: The supplied 112/2 translation reads 'liebreich zu seinem Volke'; 'liebrich' is a misspelling.
